title: Information Technology Act, 2000
source: curated summary - authentic text at the India Code URL

sections.heading: Penalty and compensation for damage to computer system
sections.text: Civil liability for unauthorised access, downloading, introduction of contaminants, damage, disruption, denial of access or tampering.

sections.heading: Compensation for failure to protect data
sections.text: A body corporate handling sensitive personal data that is negligent in maintaining reasonable security practices is liable to pay compensation.

sections.heading: Tampering with computer source documents
sections.text: Knowingly concealing, destroying or altering computer source code required to be kept by law.

sections.heading: Computer related offences
sections.text: Dishonestly or fraudulently doing any act referred to in section 43.

sections.heading: Punishment for identity theft
sections.text: Fraudulent or dishonest use of another person's electronic signature, password or other unique identification feature.

sections.heading: Punishment for cheating by personation using a computer resource
sections.text: Cheating by personation by means of any communication device or computer resource - the provision used for most online fraud.

sections.heading: Punishment for violation of privacy
sections.text: Intentionally capturing, publishing or transmitting the image of a private area of any person without consent.

sections.heading: Punishment for publishing obscene material in electronic form
sections.text: Publishing or transmitting obscene material in electronic form.

sections.heading: Power to issue directions for blocking public access
sections.text: The Central Government may direct blocking of information in the interest of sovereignty, security, public order and related grounds, following the prescribed procedure.

sections.heading: Exemption from liability of intermediary
sections.text: Safe harbour for intermediaries that only provide access and do not initiate, select the receiver of, or modify the transmission, subject to observing due diligence and acting on actual knowledge.
